en.headline: Police charge woman over fake Andy Hui concert tickets sold online
en.dek: A 48-year-old woman faces four counts after buyers paid about HK$20,000 for 14 invalid tickets to the Hung Hom shows.
body: Police have charged a 48-year-old woman with obtaining property by deception after she allegedly sold forged tickets for Andy Hui’s recent concerts at the Hong Kong Coliseum.

Officers said the woman posted offers on social media and arranged meet-ups in Mong Kok, Tsim Sha Tsui and Yau Ma Tei between 8 and 9 October. Six buyers paid in cash or by electronic transfer for a total of 14 tickets, losing about HK$20,000. The tickets were rejected at the venue on the concert nights of 8 and 10 October.

Police recovered several suspected counterfeit tickets. The woman was arrested in Mong Kok on 10 October and has been charged with four counts. She is due to appear at West Kowloon Magistrates’ Courts on the morning of 13 October.
Police reminded the public to buy event tickets only through official organisers or authorised channels and not to rely on photographs supplied by unknown online sellers.

zh.headline: 警方起訴48歲女子涉網售許志安演唱會假門票
zh.dek: 女子被控四項以欺騙手段取得財產，六名買家以約2萬元購買14張無效門票。
body: 警方以「以欺騙手段取得財產」罪起訴一名48歲本地女子，指她在網上出售許志安紅館演唱會的偽造門票。
警方調查顯示，有人在社交媒體刊登售票帖文，其後透過通訊軟件安排交易。六名受害人於10月8日至9日在旺角、尖沙咀及油麻地交收，以現金或電子支付購買共14張門票，損失約2萬港元。相關演唱會於10月8日及10日在紅磡香港體育館舉行，受害人入場時發現門票無效後報案。
警方在調查中檢獲多張懷疑偽造門票。被捕女子於10月10日在旺角被拘捕，已被暫控四項罪名，案件將於10月13日上午在西九龍裁判法院提堂。
警方提醒市民購買演唱會或其他活動門票時，應透過主辦單位或認可售票渠道，切勿向來歷不明的網上賣家購買，亦不應單憑門票相片判斷真偽。
